questions.question: Illustrate the contrast between maximum power point and open circuit condition using the I–V characteristics of a solar cell. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Illustrate the contrast between maximum power point and open circuit condition using the I–
  • V characteristics of a solar cell. [A][CO1]
  • Answer:
  • The performance of a solar cell is best understood using its I–V (current-voltage) characteristics
  • curve, which shows the relationship between output current and voltage under given conditions.
  • In the open circuit condition, the terminals of the solar cell are not connected to any load. As a
  • result, the current becomes zero, while the voltage reaches its maximum value known as the open
  • circuit voltage (Voc). At this point, although voltage is maximum, no power is delivered since current
  • is zero.
  • In contrast, the maximum power point (MPP) is the point on the I–V curve where the product of
  • current and voltage is maximum. This point lies between the open circuit voltage (Voc) and short
  • circuit current (Isc). At MPP , the solar cell operates at its highest efficiency and delivers maximum
  • usable power .
  • In practical PV systems, Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) techniques are used to ensure that
  • the system always operates at this optimal point despite changing environmental conditions.
  • Thus, while the open circuit condition represents maximum voltage with zero power output, the
  • maximum power point represents the most efficient operating condition with maximum power
  • delivery.

questions.question: Present the comparison between the function of a bypass diode and the condition when no bypass diode is used in a PV module. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Present the comparison between the function of a bypass diode and the condition when no
  • bypass diode is used in a PV module. [A][CO1]
  • Answer:
  • Bypass diodes are essential components used in photovoltaic modules to enhance performance and
  • protect the system under partial shading conditions.
  • A bypass diode is connected in parallel with a group of solar cells. When some cells are shaded or
  • damaged, the diode provides an alternate path for current to flow, thereby preventing reverse
  • biasing of those cells. This helps to avoid the formation of hotspots, which can damage the module.
  • It also ensures that the overall power output is not drastically reduced.
  • In the absence of a bypass diode, shaded cells behave like resistive loads and start dissipating power
  • instead of generating it. This leads to overheating, hotspot formation, and possible permanent
  • damage to the solar cells. Additionally, the overall output power of the module drops significantly.
  • Therefore, bypass diodes improve the reliability, safety, and efficiency of PV modules, especially
  • under non-uniform illumination conditions.

questions.question: Write the advantages and limitations of lithium-ion batteries compared to lead-acid batteries for solar applications. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Write the advantages and limitations of lithium-ion batteries compared to lead-acid batteries
  • for solar applications. [A][CO3]
  • Answer:
  • Battery storage plays a crucial role in solar power systems, and the choice of battery type significantly
  • affects performance and efficiency.
  • Lithium-ion batteries offer several advantages over traditional lead-acid batteries. They have a higher
  • energy density, meaning they can store more energy in a smaller size. They also have a longer
  • lifespan with more charge-discharge cycles, higher efficiency (typically 90–95%), and require minimal
  • maintenance. Additionally, they are lightweight and compact.
  • However, lithium-ion batteries have certain limitations. They have a higher initial cost and require a
  • Battery Management System (BMS) for safe operation. They are also sensitive to high temperatures
  • and need proper control systems.
  • On the other hand, lead-acid batteries are cheaper and widely available but are heavier, have lower
  • efficiency, shorter lifespan, and require regular maintenance.
  • Thus, lithium-ion batteries are more suitable for modern solar applications due to their superior
  • performance, despite their higher cost.

questions.question: Explain the factors affecting voltage drop in DC cabling / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the factors affecting voltage drop in DC cabling. [U][CO4]
  • Answer:
  • Voltage drop in DC cabling is an important factor that affects the efficiency of photovoltaic systems. It
  • occurs due to the resistance offered by the conductors as current flows through them.
  • Several factors influence voltage drop. The length of the cable plays a major role, as longer cables
  • result in higher resistance and greater voltage drop. The amount of current flowing through the
  • conductor also affects the drop, with higher current leading to increased losses. The cross-sectional
  • area of the conductor is another key factor; smaller conductors have higher resistance and hence
  • more voltage drop.
  • The material of the conductor also matters, with copper having lower resistance compared to
  • aluminum. Additionally, temperature affects resistance, as higher temperatures increase resistance
  • and thereby increase voltage drop.
  • To minimize voltage drop, proper cable sizing, shorter cable lengths, and high-quality conductive
  • materials should be used.
  • Thus, careful design of DC cabling ensures improved efficiency and reduced power losses in PV
  • systems.

questions.question: Classify the electrical and physical parameters of a PV module and explain their importance in system design. / [CO1] [5x3 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• Classify the electrical and physical parameters of a PV module and explain their importance
  • in system design. [A][CO1]
  • Answer:
  • The parameters of a photovoltaic module are broadly classified into electrical and physical
  • parameters, both of which are important for system design.
  • Electrical parameters include open circuit voltage (Voc), short circuit current (Isc), maximum power
  • (Pmax), and voltage and current at maximum power point (Vmpp and Impp). These parameters are
  • crucial for selecting compatible inverters, charge controllers, and for proper system sizing.
  • Physical parameters include the size, dimensions, weight, and mounting type of the module. These
  • factors influence installation, structural support design, and space requirements.
  • Understanding both electrical and physical parameters ensures that the PV system operates
  • efficiently and safely. Proper selection and integration of modules help achieve optimal performance
  • and long-term reliability.
  • Hence, these parameters play a vital role in the design and implementation of solar PV systems
  • [5X3=15]

questions.question: Present the differences between field measurement and STC measurement of PV module parameters, including the effect on calculated efficiency and output. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Present the differences between field measurement and STC measurement of PV module
  • parameters, including the effect on efficiency and output. [A][CO1]
  • Answer:
  • The performance of photovoltaic (PV) modules is evaluated under two main conditions:
  • Standard Test Conditions (STC) and field conditions.
  • Standard Test Conditions (STC) are controlled laboratory conditions defined as solar irradiance of
  • 1000 W/m², cell temperature of 25°C, and air mass of 1.5. These conditions provide a uniform basis
  • for comparing different PV modules and are used to specify the rated power of a module. Under STC,
  • the output values such as voltage, current, and efficiency are ideal and consistent.
  • In contrast, field measurements are taken under actual environmental conditions where parameters
  • such as solar irradiance, ambient temperature, wind speed, dust, and shading vary continuously.
  • Because of these variations, the actual performance of PV modules in the field differs significantly
  • from STC values.
  • One major factor affecting performance is temperature. As temperature increases, the open circuit
  • voltage (Voc) decreases, leading to a reduction in power output. Similarly, variations in irradiance
  • directly affect the current output of the module. Dust accumulation and partial shading also reduce
  • the effective irradiance reaching the panel surface.
  • As a result, the efficiency and output power in field conditions are usually lower than STC ratings.
  • Therefore, while STC provides a standard reference for comparison and rating, field measurements
  • reflect the real performance of the PV system.
  • Thus, understanding both STC and field conditions is essential for accurate system design,
  • performance prediction, and efficiency evaluation.

questions.question: Discuss the impact of light intensity and temperature on the output characteristics of a silicon solar cell. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the impact of light intensity and temperature on the output characteristics of a
  • silicon solar cell. [U][CO2]
  • Answer:
  • The output characteristics of a silicon solar cell are significantly influenced by environmental
  • factors, particularly light intensity (irradiance) and temperature. These factors directly affect
  • the current, voltage, and overall efficiency of the solar cell.
  • When light intensity increases, more photons strike the surface of the solar cell, resulting in the
  • generation of a greater number of electron-hole pairs. This increases the short circuit current (Isc)
  • almost linearly with irradiance. As a result, the overall power output of the solar cell also increases.
  • However, the effect of irradiance on voltage is relatively small compared to its effect on current.
  • On the other hand, temperature has an inverse effect on performance. As temperature increases, the
  • semiconductor properties of the solar cell change, leading to increased recombination of charge
  • carriers. This results in a reduction in the open circuit voltage (Voc). Since power output is a product
  • of voltage and current, the decrease in voltage leads to a reduction in overall efficiency.
  • In real conditions, high solar irradiance is often accompanied by high temperature. While increased
  • irradiance tends to increase power output, the simultaneous rise in temperature reduces efficiency.
  • Therefore, the net effect depends on the balance between these two factors.
  • To improve performance, proper system design should include adequate ventilation and cooling
  • mechanisms to reduce temperature rise.
  • Thus, while higher light intensity enhances power generation, increased temperature negatively
  • affects efficiency, making thermal management crucial in PV systems.

questions.question: Illustrate the proper charging and discharging procedure to maximize battery life. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Illustrate the proper charging and discharging procedure to maximize battery life. [A][CO3]
  • Answer:
  • Battery life in solar energy systems is greatly influenced by proper charging and discharging practices.
  • Efficient battery management ensures long lifespan, reliable performance, and reduced maintenance
  • costs.
  • During the charging process, it is important to use a suitable charge controller such as PWM (Pulse
  • Width Modulation) or MPPT (Maximum Power Point Tracking). These controllers regulate the voltage
  • and current supplied to the battery, preventing overcharging. Overcharging can lead to excessive
  • heat generation, electrolyte loss (in lead-acid batteries), and internal damage. Charging should be
  • done in stages such as bulk, absorption, and float to ensure complete and safe charging.
  • During the discharging process, deep discharge should be avoided as it significantly reduces battery
  • life. Each battery has a recommended Depth of Discharge (DoD), and exceeding this limit can cause
  • permanent damage. Maintaining a moderate discharge level improves cycle life and efficiency.
  • Temperature also plays an important role. Batteries should be operated within the recommended
  • temperature range, as high temperatures accelerate chemical degradation, while very low
  • temperatures reduce capacity.
  • Regular maintenance, including checking electrolyte levels (for lead-acid batteries), cleaning
  • terminals, and monitoring voltage levels, is essential for optimal performance.
  • Thus, by following proper charging stages, avoiding deep discharge, and maintaining suitable
  • operating conditions, the lifespan and efficiency of batteries can be significantly improved.

questions.question: Explain the procedure for designing an effective grounding system for a substation or industrial installation. / [CO4] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the procedure for designing an effective grounding system for a substation or
  • industrial installation. [U][CO4]
  • Answer:
  • An effective grounding system is essential for ensuring the safety of personnel and equipment in
  • substations and industrial installations. It provides a low-resistance path for fault currents and helps
  • maintain system stability.
  • The design process begins with soil resistivity measurement, which determines the ability of the
  • ground to conduct electrical current. This is typically done using methods such as the Wenner four-
  • pin method. The results help in selecting the type and depth of grounding electrodes.
  • Next, a grounding grid (earth mat) is designed. This consists of a network of conductors buried in the
  • ground, arranged in a grid pattern. The grid ensures uniform distribution of fault current and reduces
  • potential differences across the surface.
  • Grounding electrodes, such as rods, plates, or pipes, are then installed deep into the soil to achieve
  • low resistance. These electrodes are connected to the grid to enhance conductivity.
  • All electrical equipment, structures, and metallic parts are properly bonded to the grounding system
  • to ensure that they remain at the same potential, thereby preventing electric shock hazards.
